submission.text: will have one RD wide BAA to monitor on SAM.gov instead of multiple BAAs across the Directorate • Why do we need another contracting tool separate from DETER? • Selecting the right contracting tool for the job leads to the best outcomes. TACTICAL BAA fills a gap for pursuing FAR-based awards for 6.1-6.4 efforts that was not available previously at the directorate level. TACTICAL will complement other tools such as the DETER ARA, SBIR/STTRs, and grants & cooperative agreements under the upcoming RAD Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA). • What if a technically qualified offeror wants to join a Topic Area Group, but missed the normal deadline? • The offeror can either wait and submit during the next annual period (every January) or AFRL can choose to release an interim request for additional executive summaries. • Will these slides be available online or via email? •The slide will be emailed to all registered participants, along with the Q&A, and will also be posted to the sam.gov DETER Virtual Industry Day announcement. • When will the next closed call be released? •Please keep monitoring the TACTICAL SAM.gov posting and sign up for notification of changes. This will notify you when there are changes or a Call announcement is made under TACTICAL. AFRL-2023-4752 Approved

GENERAL INTENT The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and incidentals necessary to furnish and install a Building Automation System (BAS) to support integration and monitoring of existing building systems at the Guam Community-Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) and the American Samoa CBOC. This project is a straight-to-construction (StC) NRM project and is intended to implement a scalable BAS architecture focused on monitoring and alarming, with future capability to expand into full control wit

ance outages and costs, enhance energy management capabilities, and strengthen VAPIHCS’s ability to maintain safe, high reliability organization (HRO) across geographically dispersed locations. Due to the remote nature of these sites and limited availability of on-island technical resources, the absence of BAS currently delays detection and response to system failures, increasing the risk of impacts to clinical operations. A BAS mitigates these risks by providing early detection and alarming of system anomalies, improving preventive maintenance timeliness, reducing system downtime, and supporting compliance with environmental and operational requirements for healthcare spaces. Centralized remote monitoring will allow VAPIHCS FMS to proactively manage building systems and coordinate off-island technical support without reliance on emergency site visits, improving continuity of care and overall facility resilience. 2. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 5pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 9 Sep 2029, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY25 by 30 NOV 2024 FY26 by 30 NOV 2025 FY27 by 30 NOV 2026 FY28 by 30 NOV 2027 FY29 by 30 NOV 2028 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. Supplemental OCI Policy: In addition, AFRL has a supplemental OCI policy that prohibits contractors/performers from concurrently providing Scientific Engineering Technical Assistance (SETA), Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS) or similar support services and being a technical performer. Therefore, as part of the FAR 9.5 disclosure requirement above, an offeror must affirm whether the offeror or any proposed team member (subawardee, consultant) is providing SETA, A&AS, or similar support to any AFRL office(s) under: (a) a current award or subaward; or (b) a past award or subaward that ended within one calendar year prior to the proposal’s submission date. If SETA, A&AS, or similar support is being or was provided to any AFRL office(s), the proposal must include: . The name of the AFRL office receiving the support; . The prime contract number; . Identification of proposed team member (subawardee, consultant) providing the support; and . An OCI mitigation plan in accordance with FAR 9.5. b. Government Procedures: In accordance with FAR 9.503, 9.504 and 9.506, the Government will evaluate OCI mitigation plans to avoid, neutralize or mitigate potential OCI issues before award and to determine whether it is in the Government’s interest to grant a waiver. TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENTS: The Air Force Research Laboratory is soliciting white papers under this Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to process and exploit multi-source, multi-domain classified, open source, non-traditional source data to improve Battlespace Awareness, derive decision quality information, and automate analysis/decision processes. Further, this BAA seeks capabilities for the discovery and analysis of emerging activities across multiple domains (ground, air, maritime, space and cyberspace) and to reduce the time needed to search and correlate data from multiple sources on multiple systems. Methods are needed to: Provide richer and more robust patterns of life to support timely, effective and efficient command and control and decisions. Characterize, locate and compare/contrast activities, driving rapid data exploration and discovery of significant events. Anticipate events by building a deep understanding of the networks that give rise to specific incidents. deliverables_scope.text: operates ship and tow simulation capabilities in support of USACE navigation, coastal, and hydraulics missions. ERDC requires a contracting framework to augment its maritime simulation capabilities through collaboration with qualified entities outside the USACE. The contemplated requirement may be structured as a MATOC. Task orders may require support for ship simulation studies, simulator database development, vessel modeling, environmental modeling, visual database development, simulation testing, data analysis, technical documentation, training, simulator design support, software/hardware integration, and technical support. 3. Anticipated Scope of Work The contractor shall be capable of providing non-personal services to support ERDC ship, tow, and watercraft simulation activities. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to, the following: a. Maritime Simulation Study Support The contractor shall be capable of defining project problem sets and solution parameters; planning and conducting simulation studies; supporting feasibility and Pre-Construction Engineering and Design level studies; coordinating with professional mariners; and supporting ERDC oversight of simulation testing. b. Simulator Database Development The contractor shall demonstrate experience developing maritime si

et; Model validation using field data and professional mariner participation; and Delivery of databases, models, and project-specific data to the Government. c. Simulation Testing and Analysis The contractor shall be capable of conducting simulation testing to evaluate navigation designs, vessel maneuvering, safety, and operational feasibility. Analysis may include vessel track plots, heat maps, throttle and rudder usage, tug usage, maneuver feasibility, and safety assessments. d. Technical Reports and Documentation The contractor shall be capable of preparing, authoring, developing, and editing technical reports, project documentation, task requirements, software/hardware requirements, training materials, multimedia materials, web-based documentation, and other deliverables in support of ERDC simulation studies. e. Simulator System Support The contractor shall be capable of supporting ship/tow simulator hardware and software systems, including system assessments, hardware/software vetting, network architecture, installation, integration, validation, system optimization, maintenance, updates, refreshes, replacement, and technical troubleshooting. f. sla_onsite.text: Printing's (BEP) Facility located in Washington, DC contains an Industrial Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WWPP). BEP's objective is to procure contractor services to manage, operate, maintain supplies and perform maintenance and provide technical support for the Wastewater and Storm Water Programs. The WWPP requires services to support the BEP on a 24/7 basis. The WWPP currently consists of four (4) systems: (1) Wiping Solution Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WSWPP), (2) Plating Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (PWPP), (3) Grease Trap Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (GTWPP), and (4) Wiping Solution Recycling Plant (WSRP). The WWPP includes an on-site lab and a materials storage area. ies for Rapid Adoption (ASTRA) ARA NUMBER: ARA FA8750-23-S-7007 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) Number: N/A I. TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENTS: The Air Force Research Laboratory is soliciting white papers under this Advanced Research Announcement (ARA) for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to enable the rapid integration of Systems of Systems (SoS) and the auto generation of tests of the System-of-systems Technology Integration Tool Chain for Heterogeneous Electronic Systems (STITCHES) subsystem specifications and properties. White papers shall: Describe methods to develop, implement, and demonstrate a software prototype of a SoS that will provide increased military effectiveness, cost leverage (i.e., the cost of the opponent to counter relative to the cost of the U.S. to deploy), and adaptability relative to the current platform-centric approach; Outline the development and provide a system architecting approach to achieve rapid integration of new U.S. technologies as they are developed, without requiring significant re-engineering of existing capabilities, systems, or systems of systems; Outline how to implement applicable Open System Architect

operate (ATO) issued by the Department of Defense (DoD); Provide system-level user identity and access management, and application-level single sign-on (SSO); Establish a repository and backup and restore all ecosystem data; Develop a graphical user interface system for web-based utilization of the toolchain and users with limited toolchain experience; and Design, implement, and integrate secure cloud-based hosting in multiple levels and provide the ability for the secure transfer of files between different levels.
